title: Critical Software enters the pilot on its regulated verticals alone, with its stack never researched
content:
Critical Software's priority-4 rank was produced mechanically. The row came from the provisional tail of the v2 ranking and was rescored using size and slot occupancy only, with no v3 evidence pass, so the flag defers the actual decision to an OSS-portfolio screen that has not yet been run.

The substantive content of the row is its vertical list: aerospace, defence, automotive, rail, finance and energy. That is an unusually consistent set of heavily regulated sectors, and it is the only reason the firm is in the pool. Against that, the tool field reads "not researched" — meaning one of the two inputs the mechanical rescore relied on, slot occupancy, was scored without any record of which platforms the firm actually delivers on.

That gap is worth naming precisely, because the record cannot distinguish an open platform slot from an unresearched one. Both look the same in the data and they point at opposite actions. Resolving which of the two applies to Critical Software is a desk task, and it should happen before the firm competes for outreach effort against leads whose stacks are known.
